questions.question: Which of the following are checked exceptions in Java?
options: NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, IllegalArgumentException
IOException, SQLException, ClassNotFoundException
StackOverflowError, OutOfMemoryError
RuntimeException, ArithmeticException, NumberFormatException
explanations: These are unchecked exceptions (they inherit from RuntimeException).
Correct. IOException, SQLException and ClassNotFoundException are checked exceptions that must be handled or declared.
Errors are not checked exceptions; they represent serious system failures.
These are unchecked exceptions that inherit from RuntimeException.

questions.question: Which of the following are unchecked exceptions?
options: IOException, FileNotFoundException, ParseException
NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
ClassNotFoundException, NoSuchMethodException
SocketException, ConnectException
explanations: These are checked exceptions from the java.io and java.text packages.
Correct. NullPointerException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inherit from RuntimeException and do not require mandatory handling.
These are checked exceptions that require try-catch or throws.
These are network checked exceptions that require explicit handling.

questions.question: What does the finally block do in Java?
options: It runs only when there is no exception in the try block
It always runs, whether there is an exception or not, after the try-catch block
It runs only when a specific exception is caught
It replaces the catch block and is used to close connections
explanations: The finally block always runs, not only when there is no exception.
Correct. The finally block always runs after the try-catch, regardless of whether an exception occurred or not.
Finally does not depend on catching exceptions; it runs in any case.
Finally does not replace catch; it complements the try-catch.

questions.question: Can you have a try block without catch in Java?
options: No, you must always have at least one catch
Yes, as long as a finally block is included
Only if throws is declared in the method signature
No, a try without catch always generates a compilation error
explanations: That is not correct; try can work without catch if it has finally.
Correct. In Java, try can be used without catch as long as a finally block is included to handle resource cleanup.
Declaring throws does not replace the need for catch or finally.
It does not generate an error if finally is included.

questions.question: What is try-with-resources in Java?
options: A try block that uses less memory than a normal try
A mechanism that automatically closes resources that implement AutoCloseable
A way to reuse exceptions across multiple try blocks
A pattern for creating resources without using constructors
explanations: Try-with-resources has no relation to memory consumption.
Correct. try-with-resources automatically closes any resource that implements the AutoCloseable interface when leaving the block, invoking the close() method.
Try-with-resources has no relation to exception reuse.
Try-with-resources is used to declare and close resources, not to create them without constructors.
